metadata.title: Pick Your Pebble
metadata.topic: AGENTIC CASEBOOK · VIDEO 1 — PICK YOUR PEBBLE
metadata.purpose: Teach the METHOD of selecting a red-team target: the fast filter, the fastest-path heuristic, why caring about the system is the honesty floor, and the six-bullet Dossier that anchors everything else. Source: books/computational-skepticism-for-ai/assignments/agentic-casebook-red-team.md (Step 1).
metadata.playlist: Doubt It When It Looks Right — The Agentic Casebook
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = a system with real actions and real consequences; TERRACOTTA = the gap between artifact and world; INK = the audit discipline; CRIMSON = the failure mode you suspect
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: no prediction-lock content (that is Video 2); no case-writing, no lens selection, no attestation. This video covers only Pebble selection and the Dossier.

beats.narration_text: Merhaba — this is Liam, in for Bear. Everything in the audit is inert until you have a system to point at. Step one: pick your Pebble. A Pebble is a real agentic AI system you will red-team — one that acts, not just talks.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Merhaba, Liam.' in EB Garamond serif above the composer
command line types in: 'Everything in the audit is inert until you have a system to point at.'
send button arms, running indicator spins
output lines appear: 'A Pebble acts. Not just talks.' / 'Step one: pick yours.'

props.command: Everything in the audit is inert until you have a system to point at.
output: A Pebble acts — sends, edits, calls, posts.
Not just a chatbot. An agent with a tool surface.

beats.narration_text: Before you name it, run the fast filter. Four gates. Any gate fails, pick again. Agentic — it acts. Blast radius — a wrong action costs something real. Safe to poke — sandboxed, yours, or a documented public case. Right-sized — one workflow, five to eleven cases.

Agentic card springs in — zap icon, label 'Agentic', sub 'acts: sends, edits, calls, posts' — on narration cue 'Agentic'
Blast Radius card springs in — shield-alert icon — on 'Blast radius'
Safe to Poke card springs in — lock icon — on 'Safe to poke'
Right-Sized card springs in — ruler icon — on 'Right-sized'

items.label: Blast Radius

beats.motion_claim: FormBCard karaoke reveal — 4 icon panels spring in sequentially on narration cues: Agentic (t=4.8s), Blast Radius (t=7.5s), Safe to Poke (t=10.0s), Right-Sized (t=12.5s)

beats.narration_text: The fastest path to done: use something you already run. Dog-food it — your email agent, your coding assistant. Or reconstruct a documented public failure, an Agents of Chaos case from the book. That sidesteps the authorization question entirely. You audit the record, not a live system you are not cleared to poke.

show.event: cream canvas; 'FASTEST PATH TO DONE' draws in serif at top
Y-fork branches: left arm draws in — teal — label 'DOG-FOOD IT'
right arm draws in — ink — label 'RECONSTRUCT A PUBLIC CASE'
sub-labels appear: 'you already run it' left; 'documented Agents of Chaos failure — no auth question' right
both paths converge at terracotta circle: 'YOUR PEBBLE'

production_viz.label: two paths to a Pebble — converge at YOUR PEBBLE
production_viz.mechanic: Y-fork layout on cream. Top label 'FASTEST PATH TO DONE' in EB Garamond. Left branch (teal arrow): 'DOG-FOOD IT' with sub 'you already run it'. production_viz.note: motion is the fork drawing and converging — the shape encodes the choice; terracotta circle is the ONE accent

beats.narration_text: This lives or dies on the honesty floor. If you do not care about the system, you will trust 'email sent' and stop. Caring is what keeps you checking the actual sent folder instead of the report. Caring is what makes the audit real.

show.event: two zones: left ARTIFACT block — document with '✓ email sent' in ink — right WORLD block — open folder icon, 'actual sent folder'
gap between them labeled 'THE HONESTY FLOOR' in serif
WITHOUT CARING path: arrow stops at artifact, crimson X — label 'trust the report'
WITH CARING path: arrow crosses gap to world, teal checkmark — label 'check the world'

production_viz.label: artifact vs world — the honesty floor
production_viz.mechanic: Two side-by-side zones on cream canvas. Left: ARTIFACT zone — a rectangle labeled 'SUCCESS REPORT' with a green check '✓ email sent'. Right: WORLD zone — a folder icon labeled 'ACTUAL SENT FOLDER'. Gap between them labeled 'THE HONESTY FLOOR' in EB Garamond serif. First: without-caring arrow (crimson) stops at artifact with X label 'trust the report'. Then: with-caring arrow (teal) crosses the gap to world with checkmark label 'check the world'. The crossing arrow is the motion.
production_viz.note: the gap is the subject — caring is what makes you cross it; the crimson/teal contrast is the whole argument

beats.narration_text: Once it passes the filter, write the Dossier. Six bullets, one page. This is the anchor every case in your casebook references.

'Six bullets, one page.' springs in as body line
'The anchor everything references.' springs in

beats.narration_text: Name. Architecture in two sentences. And the tool surface — the actual actions it can take. Not the documentation. The actions.

beats.narration_text: Deployment context — where it runs and for whom. Your candidate failure mode: your hunch about where it lies to you, on record now, before you look. And access constraints — what you can and cannot see.

beats.narration_text: The artifact is not the world. Your candidate failure mode is your hunch about where the system lies to you. The audit is checking that hunch against reality. Write the Dossier. Write the failure mode. Then start checking.

'LIES?' overlaid on artifact in terracotta — one accent moment
gap draws in, labeled 'THE ONE DISCIPLINE' in serif

Center gap: a vertical dashed separator labeled 'THE ONE DISCIPLINE' in EB Garamond. Right: WORLD — a magnifying-glass icon labeled 'ACTUAL STATE'. Draw-on order: artifact left, lies? overlay, gap separator, world right. Serif annotation below center: 'Your hunch names the gap.'

beats.narration_text: One Pebble. Four gates. Six bullets. Your candidate failure mode on the record before you look. That is your foundation.

show.event: ClaudeVerdictArtifact: artifact window opens on cream; title 'Pick Your Pebble' in serif

full artifact card holds on screen

artifactLines: Pebble: agentic, meaningful blast radius, authorized, right-sized.
Dossier: name, architecture, tool surface, context, failure mode, access.
Your hunch about where it lies to you — on the record before you look.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: 'Name your system. Two sentences on its architecture. List its tool surface — the actual actions it can take.' Not the README. The actions. That list names where the blast radius lives. If you can name the list, you can audit it. Liam, in for Bear.
